what_was_tried: 1. SEPARABLE DEST-PULL GATHER (the prompt-implied cheap shift): out[i,j]=c5[refl_row[i],refl_col[j]] via two Gathers. RESULT: 0/3000 truth. Reason: 48.7% of pairs have gray on BOTH row-sides of the bbox (matches the don't-do log's 43.5%/0-266). A separable rank-1 dest-pull selects one source per destination and also injects spurious cross-terms; the true rule is a source-scatter where outside cells above AND below land inside.

2. FIXED PAD/SLICE TRANSLATION SHIFT (the prompt's central radical lever): RULED OUT analytically. The prompt assumed brow=3 makes the vertical reflection a near-constant offset (<=2 cases). MEASURED: because the 50% xpose flag swaps rows<->cols, the ROW bbox sees both the tall-span (brow-anchored) AND the wide-span (bcol-anchored, bcol in [2,5], wide in [5,7]). Result: rmin in {2,3,4,5}, rmax in {6,7,8,9,10,11} -> 14 DISTINCT (rmin,rmax) pairs and 14 distinct row reflection vectors (identical 14 for columns). A static Pad/Slice translation cannot encode a data-dependent reflection that varies 14 ways and reflects about a variable edge. This is the key prompt-staleness finding.

3. GRIDSAMPLE single-grid reflection (collapse R_mat+C_mat to one 450-param grid): RULED OUT. GridSample grid would have to be BUILT from the data-dependent rmin/rmax (not a constant), re-materialising a >=450 F32 grid intermediate plus the build arithmetic, and GridSample is float-only -> no net win over the two F16 matrices.
4. AGGRESSIVE BOOL-collapsed reflection-matrix warp (best-exact, BUILT + measured + truth-verified): cost 6110 (predictor) / 6179 (real). 600/600 truth. This is the warp family's measured floor.

warp_family_floor_proof.irreducible_warp_memory: Any data-dependent-reflection-via-canvas needs 5 unavoidable dense tensors: R_mat[15,15]F16=450 + C_mat[15,15]F16=450 (row & col reflections differ; Einsum/MatMul are float-only so no BOOL) + c5_in F16=450 + c5_out F16=450 + color30_u8 canvas[1,1,30,30]=900 = 2700B, before the red plane + bbox arithmetic (~660B). Floor ~3360B memory + params >= ~6100 total (matches measured).
warp_family_floor_proof.why_scatter_wins: Aditya's 3857 sets output = ScatterND(input, ...) so BOTH input and output are FREE (uncounted). It writes ONLY the 270 changed cells: delta_updates[270]F32=1080B mem + final_indices[270,4]=1080 par. It never materialises the 900B canvas, the two 450B reflection matrices, or the 450B reflected-gray plane. The warp family is forced to build a full canvas (Equal-tail) or full matrices (Einsum) that the sparse scatter structurally avoids.
warp_family_floor_proof.no_third_option: A data-dependent reflection must either (a) enumerate moved cells as an index list -> that IS the 3857 scatter, or (b) apply a dense permutation matrix -> the 6179 warp, or (c) a separable Gather -> proven 0/3000. There is no fourth primitive that is both a data-dependent bbox-edge reflection AND avoids materialising a canvas/matrix/index-table.
warp_family_floor_proof.free_output_dodge_checked: Trying output=Where/ScatterND directly onto the free input (to skip the 900B canvas) just relocates the gray to data-dependent destinations -> collapses back to the 270-cell scatter (3857) or needs the matrices. v1's BOOL-Concat 10-channel assembly already measured 8319 (worse). The U8 canvas + Equal is the cheapest output assembly for the warp family.
warp_family_floor_proof.competitor_corroboration: 32 public competitor task154.onnx scanned: correct graphs are 74346+, only cost-0/63 stubs go lower (zero-weight memorization lookups, score 0 hidden, traps section 14e). No public correct graph beats 3857.

prompt_staleness_findings: FINDING 1 (baseline source): extract_task.py 154 returns the 29015 OneHot/MatMul/Conv graph (opset 10, 46 nodes), NOT the 3857 Aditya scatter. The prompt says 'Baseline: extract_task.py 154 ... (cost 3857)' -- the extracted graph is NOT the 3857 floor. The 3857 floor lives only in the (un-mounted) OnnxlyFans Team_Best and the task154.md proof. AB-vs-live in this sandbox would compare against 29015, not 3857.

FINDING 2 (the radical lever's premise is stale): the prompt/lever claim 'brow=3 FIXED -> reflection is a vertical mirror about a near-constant box mid-line, tall in {8,9} gives <=2 cases, branch <=2 vertical offsets by box-side flags' is WRONG once the 50% xpose is accounted for. xpose swaps rows<->cols, so the row axis also carries the bcol/wide-driven span. Measured: 14 distinct row reflection vectors AND 14 distinct col reflection vectors -- not <=2. A <=2-offset Pad/Slice shift cannot implement this.
FINDING 3 (decoded rule IS correct): the task154.md reflect-across-nearest-bbox-side rule is exactly right (3000/3000 sim). The prompt's rule decode is accurate; only its cost-lever premise is stale.

FINDING 4 (not the 'wrong family' the reviewer feared): the prompt warns the v6 6179 lineage is the WRONG family. That label is formulation-relative (it golfs the stale 29015 LIVE). As a GRAPH, the v6/Einsum reflection IS the shift/warp family the prompt asked to test, it is CORRECT (600/600 truth), and 6179 is its genuine floor -- which is exactly what proves the warp family loses to 3857.
